Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 series this September, as usual, but the way the products are released this fall will echo the unusual circumstances of the iPhone launch during the COVID-19 pandemic in several ways.

How this fall's iPhone unveiling will differ from Apple's usual practice

Apple has many very successful products, but the iPhone has always been its crown jewel and accounts for a large share of the company's overall revenue.

It is therefore understandable that Apple strives to keep its iPhone launches consistent. By maintaining a predictable new iPhone rollout schedule, Apple is better able to keep both Wall Street and customers happy.

Generally, Apple unveils new iPhones in early September—usually four new models—and ships them all later in September.

But 2020 was an exception because of COVID-19-related reasons.

The fall 2020 iPhone lineup wasn't announced until October, and only two of the new models shipped initially, with the other two delayed until November.

This year, rumors suggest we will see some similar irregularities in Apple's release schedule.

While the September event is still expected to take place, Apple may not release all new iPhone models at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models may be available for purchase initially: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable model, the iPhone Ultra, is expected to be unveiled in September, but rumors suggest its release date may be slightly delayed, possibly not arriving until a few weeks after the Pro models launch.

Apple may also diverge from its usual practice in terms of the total number of iPhone models.

If rumors prove true that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are pushed back to a spring 2027 release, only three new models will debut this fall. This would be the smallest fall iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether due to strategic considerations, challenges from the global memory crisis, or the difficulties of mass-producing an entirely new foldable device, Apple's fall 2026 event could replay several scenarios from 2020.

What would you like to see Apple bring to this fall's iPhone event? Let us know in the comments.
